questions.question: What is a dense embedding?
options: A graph over documents
A sparse weight per vocab token — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
A token-level alignment matrix
One fixed-size vector per text where cosine similarity ranks passages by semantic proximity
questions.explanation: Dense embeddings give one vector per text (typically 384-3072 dim); cosine ranks similarity.

questions.question: What does Matryoshka Representation Learning enable?
options: Multilingual training
Faster softmax
Truncating a trained embedding to its first N dimensions and getting a still-useful smaller embedding
Cross-encoder rescoring, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
questions.explanation: Matryoshka training makes the first N dims of the vector standalone-useful, enabling cheap truncation.

questions.question: How do multi-vector (ColBERT) embeddings score query-doc pairs?
options: Cosine of mean-pooled token vectors, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
Cross-entropy
Earth-mover's distance
MaxSim: for each query token find the most similar document token, then sum the maxima
questions.explanation: ColBERT-style late interaction uses MaxSim across per-token vectors.

questions.question: What does BGE-M3 output simultaneously?
options: Only a sparse vector
Only a dense vector
Dense, sparse, and multi-vector (colbert) representations from one model in a single inference
Only a colbert vector, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
questions.explanation: BGE-M3 emits three retrieval modes from one model, useful for fused hybrid scoring.

questions.question: Why must you re-normalize a Matryoshka-truncated vector before cosine similarity?
options: Truncation breaks training
Truncation changes the vector norm; without re-normalizing, dot product no longer equals cosine
Cosine ignores normalization — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
Required by FAISS only
questions.explanation: Re-normalizing after truncation restores unit norm so dot product equals cosine again.

questions.question: Why do BGE models often need a query-side prefix string?
options: To compress queries
Required by FAISS
BGE was trained with an explicit query prompt; omitting it costs 3-5 points recall
Prefixes change tokenizer behavior, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: BGE models expect a 'Represent this sentence for searching...' prefix on queries.
